name: Stop severe bleeding
summary: Hard, uninterrupted direct pressure on the wound, escalating to a tourniquet for a limb that will not stop.
time: 10 minutes of held pressure before you reassess

steps.text: Get the wound above the level of the heart if the injury allows it, and expose it — you cannot press on what you cannot see.
Press hard, directly on the bleeding point, with the heel of your hand and a cloth if you have one.
steps.why: Pressure works by holding the vessel shut long enough for a clot to form. Pressure spread over a wide area does not close a vessel.

steps.text: Hold for a full ten minutes by the clock without lifting to look.
steps.why: Every peek tears the forming clot off and restarts the ten minutes.

steps.text: If blood soaks through, add cloth ON TOP and keep pressing. Do not remove the soaked layer.
For a limb still bleeding heavily despite pressure, apply a tourniquet 5-7 cm above the wound, never over a joint. Tighten until the bleeding STOPS, note the time, and do not loosen it.
For a wound in a junction the tourniquet cannot reach (groin, armpit, neck), pack the wound cavity tight with cloth and press down hard on the packing.

verify: Bleeding has stopped, not merely slowed.
After a tourniquet, the pulse below it is gone — a tourniquet tight enough to hurt but not tight enough to stop the pulse increases blood loss.
limits: This controls EXTERNAL bleeding. It does nothing for internal bleeding, which has no first-aid answer and needs surgery.
A tourniquet buys time at the cost of the limb's circulation. It is the right trade against bleeding to death and the wrong one against anything less.
Nothing in this corpus replaces getting to medical care. Stopping the bleeding is step one of a longer problem.
cautions: Do not use a tourniquet narrower than about 4 cm — a cord or wire cuts tissue instead of compressing the vessel.
Write the time of application somewhere on the casualty. The clock is what a clinician needs first.
Elevation and pressure points are adjuncts, not substitutes for direct pressure.
